title: LuminaryEdge — Contextual AI inference discovery
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
summary: Discovery call to understand LuminaryEdge real-time contextualization use case: high-throughput customer support augmentation with long context (40k+ tokens), multilingual support, and tool calling to fetch internal KB. Evaluated tradeoffs for Redwood Hosted, Dedicated and Private. Agreed next steps: run a short benchmark on their 32k context prompts, send security pack, and propose pricing for a pilot on dedicated capacity.
action_items: Jamie (Redwood) - Share Redwood security pack (SOC2, ISO docs) and KMS integration notes - due 2026-07-22
Rachel (Redwood) - Provide benchmark template and example prompt set for 32k context test - due 2026-07-23
Marcus (LuminaryEdge) - Provide representative prompt corpus and access to a masked KB sample for tool-calling POC - due 2026-07-24
next_steps: Schedule 1-hour tech bench (SE-led) the week of 2026-07-27 to run 32k context benchmarks
Pricing proposal for 4-week dedicated pilot (baseline throughput + burst) by 2026-07-24
Share security and deployment options doc (Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, Private)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-20 16:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Rachel (Redwood SE), Tom (Redwood SE remote), Marcus (CTO, LuminaryEdge), Priya (ML Eng), Ana (SRE), Elijah (Product)

[00:00] Jamie: Alright everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off. I'm Jamie Cortez, I'm the AE on this account for Redwood Inference.
[00:06] Marcus: Hey Jamie, hey team, Marcus here. Quick point - we're trying to decide between a hosted path vs something on dedicated GPUs for our contextual support agent.
[00:14] Rachel: Hi all, Rachel Nguyen, SE. I work with latency benchmarking and model packing. We're excited to hear about your workload.
[00:20] Priya: Hi, Priya. We're mostly concerned about context window size - many tickets include long threads plus attached docs, so we need effectively 30k-60k token windows. Also multilingual: English, Spanish, Portuguese.
[00:33] Jamie: Got it. Can you outline traffic profile and SLA needs?
[00:36] Ana: We're aiming for p50 < 800ms for short queries, but for long-context summarization we can tolerate up to 3s. Throughput during peaks: about 120 reqs/min per region, global.
[00:47] Tom: ok thanks. A few quick clarifications - are you planning to use retrieval-augmented generation with a vector DB per customer?
[00:52] Marcus: Yes that's core. We'll call our internal KB via a tool-calling / function-call step to fetch documents, then pass concatenated context. We want the model to be able to call our service to fetch fresh snippets.
[01:02] Rachel: Perfect - Redwood supports structured tool-calling, streaming, and function-like payloads. We also have prefix caching for repeated patterns which helps token costs when the KB returns overlapping context.
[01:12] Priya: On models - we've evaluated a few open models internally: Llama-2 variants, Mistral-instruct, Falcon. We're also curious about MPT and some of the newer 70B+ models. Cost is a big factor — our dev budget is limited.
[01:25] Jamie: Right - we typically recommend a matrix: pick a model family that matches quality baseline, then pick deployment mode: Hosted (fast onboarding, pay-as-you-go), Dedicated (reserved GPUs, predictable throughput and lower unit cost), Private (VPC or on-prem) for strict data residency.
[01:39] Marcus: We're regulated, some PII, so we need audit logs and KMS integration. SOC 2 is a must. If we did Hosted, we'd need strong contracts and data retention policy.
[01:49] Rachel: We have SOC2 and ISO docs, SSO/SAML and RBAC. For key management we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS/GCP CMEK) on Dedicated and Private. Hosted can do envelope encryption; we'll send details.
[02:00] [02:05] Elijah: curious about quantization options - can we run 4-bit to save cost?
[02:08] Tom: Yes - our runtime supports 8-bit and Q4 variants for many model families; we run kernel selection and we can recommend quantization profiles. Note: Q4 can add minor generation artifacts for some instructions, we track quality regressions via evals.
[02:20] Priya: Are there any differences in tool-calling between Hosted and Private?
[02:24] Rachel: No difference in capabilities. The difference is network design: Private gives you control over the control plane and direct VPC peering, avoids egress; Hosted will transmit to our endpoint but we support VPC peering and private link in enterprise tiers.
[02:36] Marcus: Latency for 32k context — do you shard KV cache or stream tokens?
[02:41] Tom: We use a combination: continuous batching, KV cache locality, and chunked context streaming. For >32k we recommend model variants with extended context windows, e.g., 32k/64k families, sometimes we emulate very long context with retrieval and summary windows to keep latency down.
[02:56] Priya: Which open models do you recommend for multilingual and long context?
[02:59] Rachel: Mistral-instruct and variants are strong on instruction following but may need fine-tuning for multilingual. Llama-2-family (70B) has wide tooling but 70B is expensive. Falcon-40B/180B has good throughput; some of the newer 32k context forks are promising. We also recommend evaluating a mixed approach: smaller fast model for routing and a larger one for heavy summarization.
[03:20] Marcus: What's the pilot configuration you'd suggest?
[03:23] Jamie: For your profile, start with a 4-week Dedicated pilot: reserve a small GPU pool sized for your 120 rps peak (we'll right-size after bench). Use one 32k-context model variant in mixed precision q4 and a fallback to a higher-precision 8-bit family for quality-sensitive flows.
[03:40] Ana: For Private/on-prem, what's included? We have air-gapped infra for some clients.
[03:44] Rachel: We have a Private deployment option: customer-managed control plane with optional air-gapped installer. It includes audit logs, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations. Onboarding takes longer (couple of weeks) vs Hosted.
[03:55] Priya: Ok on prompt engineering: we will likely do function-calling where the model emits a structured JSON with fields. Any caveats?
[04:02] Tom: Our function-calling supports typed schemas, streaming structured outputs, and backoff policies if tool calls fail. We also support automatic validation and retry. One thing to watch is token budget when you pass huge JSON schemas back and forth; better to pass compact keys and lookup client-side.
[04:18] Marcus: For security, we need retention controls and the ability to disable logging for certain flows. Is that doable?
[04:23] Jamie: Yes - we support per-route logging controls and the Dedicated/Private modes can disable logging or keep logs only locally. We'll share policy options.
[04:30] Priya: Any examples of latency numbers?
[04:33] Rachel: Preliminary, for a 32k context on a optimized 70B-class model in q4 on Dedicated, p50 around 700-900ms depending on GPU type and batch. For streaming incremental responses we can get early tokens in ~200-300ms and then continue. Hosted median will be slightly higher due to multi-tenant scheduling.
[04:50] Elijah: Are there built-in evals to detect quality regressions when quantizing?
[04:54] Tom: Yes - Redwood Optimize includes regression alerts tied to prompt sets. You upload a suite, we run A/B and will flag differences exceeding thresholds.
[05:02] Marcus: Can we try a bench with our own prompts?
[05:05] Jamie: Absolutely. Rachel will own the bench template. We'll spin up a short run on Dedicated capacity or a hosted sandbox depending on contract.
[05:12] Priya: About costs - if we go Dedicated with reserved capacity, what's typical commitment?
[05:16] Jamie: Typically monthly or annual reserved commits. The pilot can be monthly with a small commit. We can show unit cost comparisons: hosted per-token vs dedicated amortized GPU cost. We'll include examples in the pricing deck.
[05:26] Marcus: Any concerns about vendor lock with Redwood? We want the ability to shift between hosted and private over time.
[05:30] Rachel: We purposefully design the API and model pinning to be consistent across modes so you can migrate: same SDKs, same model catalog, same rollout policies. Data egress and KMS keys differ but the developer experience is consistent.
[05:42] Ana: Action items: we'll prepare sample prompts and masked KB excerpt.
[05:45] Jamie: Great. Recap: Redwood to share security pack, benchmark template, pricing for 4-week dedicated pilot. LuminaryEdge to share prompt corpus and KB sample. Schedule SE bench next week.
[05:58] Marcus: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[06:01] Jamie: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with calendar invite and links.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hears (e.g., "q4" transcribed as "cue four" in some places), speaker overlap near the end.
notes: Call emphasized model selection matrix and pilot path; strong security requirements (SOC2/KMS) push leaning to Dedicated or Private for regulated flows. Customer prioritized long context (32k+) and multilingual support with tool-calling. Agreed to run a bench and share security docs.
